# SdkWork Claw Router v0.1.0

## Scope

This is the first formal release baseline for `sdkwork-clawrouter`.
There was no prior successful release to extend, so the notes below consolidate the full product baseline from the initial commit through the current release-ready state.

## What Changed

- Added runtime configuration support for server and desktop modes with OS-standard config and data locations.
- Made server deployments require PostgreSQL by default and fail fast on placeholder or missing database configuration.
- Made desktop deployments default to SQLite and auto-create the expected runtime config path.
- Added release environment generation and preflight tooling so release settings can be written and validated from a single contract.
- Added install package planning and build tooling for 24 package combinations across:
  - Windows, Linux, and macOS
  - x64 and arm64
  - archive, service, container, and desktop modes
- Added install initialization smoke coverage so the release package can be validated without launching the dev server.
- Added explicit portal/API base URL configuration for gateway, app, backend, and open API routes.
- Added delivery guardians and LFS seed checks so release validation can detect missing shared content early.
- Added release documentation under `docs/release` for future versioned records.

## Architecture Impact

- Database policy is now mode-aware:
  - server deployments default to PostgreSQL
  - desktop deployments default to SQLite
- Runtime config paths are now predictable on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Release artifacts are versioned by platform, architecture, and deployment mode, which makes downstream packaging deterministic.
- Release configuration is generated from an executable contract instead of ad hoc edits.
- The release process can be checked without starting `pnpm dev` or the edge development smoke server.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-claw-router-application.test.mjs`
- `node scripts/plan-claw-router-install-packages.mjs --check`
- `node scripts/build-claw-router-install-package.mjs --check --dry-run --all`
- `node scripts/smoke-install-package-init.mjs --check --dry-run`

## Remaining Risk

- Real binary packaging still needs a full release environment run before publishing production artifacts.
- Sibling repositories used by the workspace should remain pinned to their own committed `origin/main` revisions before release promotion.
- Release helpers and environment help text should continue to stay in sync with the runtime contract as the product evolves.
